Outcome_variable.extract_value: life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect
Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [010_22_instruments] The Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS; Diener et al., 1985) is a 5-item scale designed to measure global cognitive judgments of satisfaction with one’s life. Participants indicate their agreement with each item using a 7-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree). Higher scores indicate greater life satisfaction. The SWLS has demonstrated good psychometric properties in various populations (Diener et al., 1985; Pavot & Diener, 1993). In the current study, Cronbach’s alpha for the SWLS was .89 at Time 1 and .91 at Time 2. [010_22_instruments] The Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS; Watson et al., 1988) is a 20-item scale that measures positive affect (PA) and negative affect (NA). Participants rate the extent to which they have experienced each emotion during the past week using a 5-point Likert scale (1 = very slightly or not at all, 5 = extremely). Higher scores on the PA subscale indicate greater positive affect, and higher scores on the NA subscale indicate greater negative affect. The PANAS has shown good reliability and validity across diverse samples (Watson et al., 1988). In the current study, Cronbach’s alpha for the PA subscale was .87 at Time 1 and .88 at Time 2. For the NA subscale, Cronbach’s alpha was .85 at Time 1 and .86 at Time 2.
